record.name: Brazil
record.summary: No qualifying institute or commitment identified. PBIA action 51 provides for a national centre researching AI risks, safety, transparency and reliability and supporting systems audits; its remit to evaluate advanced models remains unresolved. The separate CEBRI and ITS Rio AISO design is a non-governmental proposal, with no government adoption found. PL 2338/2023 still awaits a rapporteur opinion in the Chamber special committee.

PBIA action 51's national research centre covers AI risks, transparency and reliability and facilitation of systems audits, but the existing question of a mandate covering advanced models remains unresolved. News search from 17 October 2026 in English and Portuguese, with the science ministry's news listing (newest 10 November), the data protection authority's sandbox listing (newest relevant item 5 November) and the Chamber of Deputies news of 4 November. Left for review: the data protection authority's listing item of 5 November on concluding its first AI sandbox and announcing a second on digital games for children, and the proposal in parliamentary bill PL 5960/2025, reported 4 November, for INSOED, an Inmetro-coordinated testing and certification network for AI and digital infrastructure. The bill did not originate with the government, the committee report was read only in part, and the listings were not paged through in full. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

check.language_note: The recorded pt queries use a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. The earlier English-search pass on 17 October 2026 left the then-recorded national or official-language coverage unchanged; the work is described below. The additional status review used Portuguese and English searches and read primary PBIA texts in both languages; the AISO report was read in English. Search batches for the additional status review, using 1-based positions in check.searches: 4, 5; 6; 7, 8. Each group records the same exact registered URLs found in its combined search results, without attribution to an individual query. Explicit page opens and finds and unverified URL variants are excluded. Groups list the recorded queries; some requests also contained additional queries retained in the research evidence.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The government's PBIA action 51 proposes an algorithmic-transparency and trustworthy-AI centre. ITS Rio and CEBRI separately authored their own AI Safety and Opportunities Institute proposal. Both retrieved sources concern Brazilian institutional options, with distinct authorship and proposals; neither alone proves the absence of a qualifying national institute.
check.governance_note: Portuguese and English PBIA texts confirm a broad risk-research and audit-support centre, while the scope covering advanced models remains unresolved. Government bill 6237/2025 would assign regulatory and advisory roles, including compliance audits. Neither text establishes a qualifying national model-evaluation designation. The independent AISO report is not treated as a government-appointed inquiry.

related_bodies.name: Centro Nacional de Transparência Algorítmica e IA Confiável (PBIA action 51)
related_bodies.role: Its remit covers research and studies on AI risks, safety, transparency and reliability, supporting systems auditing and evaluation. It is a national research centre provided for in PBIA action 51, with R$ 40 million for 2024-2028. Whether this covers evaluation of advanced models remains unresolved. The August UFMG implementation report still requires accessible primary confirmation.

related_bodies.name: Brazilian Institute for AI Safety and Opportunities (AISO), non-governmental proposal
related_bodies.role: CEBRI and ITS Rio published an institutional design on 18 September 2025. The full report describes an exploratory proposal to stimulate debate. No government appointment as an inquiry, formal government proposal or adoption was found.

related_bodies.name: ANPD and the regulatory system discussed under PL 2338/2023
related_bodies.role: ANPD handles data protection, and AI regulation is proposed. PL 2338/2023 awaits a rapporteur opinion. The government bill PL 6237/2025 joined to it proposes regulatory coordination and advisory committees. ANPD finished the tests of its first AI and data-protection sandbox, publishing the final monitoring report on 5 November 2026, and is preparing a second edition on the safe use of digital games by children and adolescents. No designation as a national institute to evaluate advanced models was established.

record.notes:
PBIA action 51 was read in Portuguese and in the official English version. Both describe research on risks, safety, transparency and reliability and support for systems audits and evaluation. This is a government centre commitment, but it does not settle the criterion of evaluating advanced models. The full CEBRI and ITS Rio AISO report describes an exploratory design to stimulate debate; no government appointment or adoption was found. The current Chamber record still shows PL 2338/2023 awaiting the special-committee rapporteur. The government's separate PL 6237/2025, submitted on 8 December 2025 and joined to that bill by order of 19 March 2026, was also read: it would provide for regulatory coordination, ANPD and sectoral-authority duties, and advisory committees. Article 8(X) concerns compliance audits, while article 8(XVIII) would let sectoral authorities and ANPD designate marketed general-purpose models and applications as materially relevant. Article 3(I) would permit support for infrastructure to assess model and application safety. These regulatory and enabling powers do not themselves designate a national institute to evaluate advanced models. ANPD's 19 August 2026 sandbox methodology describes testing transparency, explainability and personal-data protection in participant solutions. The reported August implementation of the PBIA centre remains unresolved because the Agência Gov source still returns an election-period unavailability notice, including through the single attempt to retrieve a text copy. The prior August implementation and Paris-summit sources remain cited for evidence history, not as new verification.

On 4 November 2026 the Chamber of Deputies' news agency reported a committee hearing on a deputy's bill, PL 5960/2025, which would create Insoed, a network of public and private laboratories to test, certify and create technical standards for AI and digital infrastructure. It is a parliamentary bill, not the government's own proposal.

next_check.reason: Retrieve an accessible primary act for the reported PBIA centre launch and clarify duties concerning advanced models; check PL 2338/2023 and government bill 6237/2025 for later institutional acts.
